note: Reviewed local snapshot of experimental gas-phase geometries, expressed as observation collections. Cartesian coordinates are optional: records that publish internal coordinates only are fitted by app.geometry.fitter and validated back against every observation. This file is a cache seed, not a capability gate -- app.geometry.providers.nist_cccbdb can add records at runtime without a source edit.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Experimental gas-phase T-shaped C2v structure listed by NIST CCCBDB from H. S. P. Müller et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 3, 1570 (2001). Internal coordinates: r(Cl-F eq) = 1.597 Å, r(Cl-F ax) = 1.697 Å, ∠(F ax-Cl-F eq) = 87.45°, ∠(F ax-Cl-F ax) = 174.9° (by symmetry assuming planarity).

source.comments: Equilibrium re structure from A.R. Hoy, P.R. Bunker, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 74, 1-8 (1979), as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB's experimental gas-phase geometry page.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: r(C-H) = 1.087 A (1979Hir:213); the Td H-C-H angle of 109.471 degrees follows exactly from tetrahedral symmetry (cf. 1974Sve/Kov). Cartesian coordinates as listed by NIST CCCBDB for this bond length.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Gurvich, L.V.; Veyts, I.V.; Alcock, C.B., Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, 4th ed., Hemisphere, New York, 1989, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB (gas-phase electron diffraction P-Cl axial/equatorial bond lengths). source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: K. Kuchitsu (ed.), Structure of Free Polyatomic Molecules - Basic Data, Springer, Berlin, 1998, re value, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. Cartesian coordinates as listed by CCCBDB for this bond length (Oh symmetry).

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Gurvich, L.V.; Veyts, I.V.; Alcock, C.B., Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, 4th ed., Hemisphere, New York, 1989, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB (apical/basal Br-F bond lengths, apical-basal and adjacent-basal angles). The trans-basal F-Br-F angle (169.6 degrees) is not separately tabulated by CCCBDB; it is the unique C4v-consistent value implied by the two measured angles (cos(theta_trans) = cos(2*theta_apical-basal)), included here as a derived geometric consequence, not an independent measurement.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Herzberg, G., Electronic Spectra and Electronic Structure of Polyatomic Molecules, Van Nostrand, New York, 1966, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. The two O-O bonds are equivalent by resonance/symmetry despite the Lewis structure's formal single/double bond distinction.

Gas-phase P–F axial and equatorial bond lengths. The D3h point group fixes every F–P–F angle at exactly 90, 120 or 180 degrees; CCCBDB lists no separate angle measurement.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Takami, M.; Kuze, H., Infrared-microwave double resonance spectroscopy of the SiF4 nu3 fundamental using a tunable diode laser, J. Chem. Phys. 78, 2204-2209 (1983), as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. Bond length derived from the ground-state rotational constant B0; F–Si–F angles fixed by Td symmetry.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Kuchitsu, K. (ed.), Structure of Free Polyatomic Molecules - Basic Data, Springer, Berlin, 1998, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. Cl–C–Cl angles fixed by Td symmetry.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Herzberg, G., Electronic Spectra and Electronic Structure of Polyatomic Molecules, Van Nostrand, New York, 1966, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. The central atom is C (H–C≡N); the isomer HNC is a different species.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Kuchitsu, K. (ed.), Structure of Free Polyatomic Molecules - Basic Data, Springer, Berlin, 1998, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. Equilibrium (re) bond lengths. O–C–Cl follows from Cl–C–Cl by symmetry. CCCBDB's Cartesian coordinates for this species do not reproduce these internal coordinates, so they are omitted and rebuilt from the observations.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Gurvich, L. V.; Veyts, I. V.; Alcock, C. B., Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, 4th ed., Hemisphere, New York, 1989, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. H–C–O follows from H–C–H by planar C2v symmetry, (360° − 116.133°)/2 = 121.93°; CCCBDB lists it rounded to 121.9°.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Hellwege, K.-H. and Hellwege, A. M. (eds.), Landolt-Börnstein Group II Volume 7: Structure Data of Free Polyatomic Molecules, Springer, Berlin, 1976, as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. Electron-diffraction (ra) structure.

source.name: NIST CCCBDB
source.comments: Magnuson, D. W., Microwave spectrum and molecular structure of bromine trifluoride, J. Chem. Phys. 27, 223 (1957), as tabulated by NIST CCCBDB. T-shaped C2v structure. F(ax)–Br–F(ax) = 2 × 86.21° follows from planarity.
